summary: Wooden tower by 1917 on Pocomoonshine Mountain in Princeton, Maine; two 60-foot steel towers with CCC help went up in 1934; now listed as gone.

facts.design: 60-foot steel tower with inside stairs (1934), replacing a 58-foot wood tower (1917)
facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no readable source gives a removal date or describes the site now

events.note: 58-foot wood tower constructed, per the 1917 Annual Report of the Forest Commissioner as quoted on easternuslookouts.weebly.com

corrections.why: The 1919 Maine Forest Service map and the Forest Commissioner reports as quoted use Pocomoonshine; the FFLA county list uses Poccomoonshine. Editor to confirm the usual spelling before changing the name.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLA list spells the name with a double c; the Maine map and the quoted reports use Pocomoonshine. The story uses Pocomoonshine.

notes_for_editor: Living New Deal's Pocomoonshine page (livingnewdeal.org/sites/pocomoonshine-mountain-firetower-princeton-me/) returns 403 to the cache and was read only through WebFetch, so it is not cited or machine-checked. It gives a 56-foot wood tower (1918), a 63-foot steel tower built by a CCC camp in 1934, dismantling in the 1980s, and 'No Longer Extant'. The Maine FFLA Facebook post at facebook.com/100085116022419/posts/here-is-a-shot-of-the-poccomoonshine-mountain-fire-tower-in-princeton-back-aroun/763550716492122/ says the tower was removed in fall 1978 and that only footings remain; Facebook would not open here. Both conflict with each other and with the Annual Report heights, and neither could be checked, so the story gives no removal date and no 'footings' claim. Re-check the site today if a readable source turns up. The Annual Report figures do not reconcile: the old tower is 58 feet, the new ones 60 feet, yet the report says each new tower is 15 feet higher. The story states that conflict rather than choosing one figure.
